notes:
=== PASS 1 (2026-08-29/30, interrupted by weekly limit, resumed) ===

THE BEST-DISCIPLINED WORK OF THE CAMPAIGN, and the contrast with Poly1305 is the point: this one COMMITTED its on-chip harness. 4 chip.run/load_bitstream sites and 22 stop_reason reads in the committed gate file, all reproducible from the tree. I verified: the module resolves to the worktree, 83 passed / 9 skipped exactly as reported, and the 9 skips are NOT hidden -- every one is explicitly pinned to test_KNOWN_GAP_the_scan_loop_does_not_terminate_on_chip, and that gate FAILS THE DAY THE GAP CLOSES so it cannot rot.

THE INDEPENDENT DECODER IS GENUINELY INDEPENDENT. I checked: `lz4` is NOT importable in the venv, so the builder correctly shells out to the GNU Radio interpreter where lz4.block 4.0.2 (the reference C implementation, dfsg-packaged) lives. Real chip -> real reference C decoder -> exact input returned. That is the gate the spec demanded precisely so our encoder and our decoder could not be self-consistent-but-both-wrong.

MEASURED FINDINGS (now INV-61, five clauses -- silent failures a placed panel-backed block can have):
  * TWO PANEL REGIONS THAT ALIAS RETURN A WRONG ANSWER OF THE RIGHT LENGTH. With window_words = 2**16 the hash table aliased onto history address 0: format-legal, correct length, wrong payload. INV-33's overlap hazard at the MEMORY tier.
  * MOVE DOES NOT SET FLAGS -- cost two real defects; lit=3 mat=1 emitted 0x30 for 0x31, INVISIBLE to every model gate.
  * THE INPUT LANDING RESOLVES FROM cells[0], NOT FROM `input_cell`. Pass 1 was a silent no-op with QueueEmpty and ZERO panel writes while place/route/DRC/build ALL reported success. Same family as INV-60.
  * An inherited face literal made a RUN-TIME head-on pair that the STATIC layout check correctly reported as absent -- a real limit of the INV-56 predicate I forwarded, found by using it.
  * Hash table built during pass 1 destroys compression (repetitive payload -89% -> +0.74%); the insert must happen at the position being encoded.

A MUTATION GATE THAT WAS SECRETLY A NO-OP: the MINMATCH mutant written the obvious way (lower the threshold) never fires, proven by run-length histograms {4:1,5:1,486:1} and {0:14,80:1} -- NEVER 1-3, because the candidate comes from a 4-byte hash. It must TRUNCATE, not lower a threshold. This is INV-4's own failure mode: a mutant that cannot fail proves nothing.

MEASURED DEAD END: 're-fold as a serpentine' does NOT work. With a max-hop term, ~500 restarts x 3 shapes at K=6,7 still needed ELEVEN hops; the 36-edge graph with four 4-way hubs forces it. A merged ADDR+RET would remove 5 edges but is 41 instructions against 31 words. That is why the next move is graph-shrinking, not layout search.

IT ALSO FIXED A DEFECT IN THE SHIPPED DECODER'S SUITE: the 'random' payload re-seeded per element, yielding 2000 copies of ONE byte. A random-data gate that tested no randomness.

MODEL-LEVEL RESULTS: all 10 payload classes round-trip under the golden AND are accepted by the independent decoder with exact bytes; random x5 seeds pass; incompressible expansion 0.45% against the 0.5% bound. Three INV-4 format mutants each proven to fail. The on-chip gate proven BY MUTATION (baseline PASS -> both mutants CAUGHT -> restored PASS).

GATES: full sweep 1265 passed / 99 skipped / 0 failed. placekyt/tests 1219 -- I re-ran it myself post-merge, exact baseline. gen_dashboard --check clean. No engine or router file touched. Merge conflicts were KB-only (both sides appended); resolved keeping both, INV-61 assigned at landing.

=== PASS 2 (2026-08-30, claude-fable-5) — DONE ===

PASS 1'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, PROVEN BY TRACE. enable_trace() + per-cell exec_tick counts against the model's expected counts showed to_hash at hop 11 landed EXACTLY ON HASH (not out of the footprint), and the EventLimit was an INFINITE RE-PROBE of position 0, not ring saturation: RET dispatched 1596x while MATCH executed once. TWO real defects: (1) the no-candidate miss path had NO i += 1; (2) NO CELL EVER ISSUED THE HASH-TABLE INSERT — the slot stayed empty forever. The suspected setph race was measured SAFE (450 ns margin under full livelock congestion).

BUILT: 14 -> 15 cells. The 12-cell ring KEPT deliberately (the scan is a genuine cycle closed by the panel return) but re-ordered frequency-weighted: per-position edges ride 1-6 hops (RET->HASH 11->6, HASH->ADDR ->1 by abutment, VERIFY->SEQ miss ->1 by west flip); the per-sequence formatter takes the long arcs; now a pinned gate. New INS cell = second panel client speaking the RAW panel register protocol through the controller, insert commit DEFERRED to the next probe (panel-visible order identical to the model). RET distinguishes the slot return by COUNTING (4+1 reads/position).

DONE MEANS: all 12 payload classes (0-2000 bytes, tail AND scan) byte-exact against the model on the placed+routed+built chip, round-trip, accepted by the independent reference C decoder. 83/9-skipped -> 109/0. The KNOWN_GAP gate fired and was deleted; its 9 pinned skips un-skipped. Incompressible expansion 0.45% and repetitive -> 10.7% both measured ON CHIP.

MEASURED DEAD ENDS (in KB): insert through the controller's entries wedges on a mid-port-burst stall (n=492 died at position 3, n=416 completed — same program); commit-after-read wedges at position 125; ADDR-hosted insert 28-34 instructions vs 22-word budget. Plus a genuine SIMULATOR-BRIDGE ARTIFACT: the panel drops a held-ack release when a run(max_events) boundary lands in the capture window — the harness pump re-issues it.

MUTATION-PROOF: three ON-CHIP INV-4 mutants each proven to fire, including the ACTUAL pass-1 defect. The dead-insert mutant still round-trips (all-literals is legal) and is caught by the on-chip RATIO gate, which exists for exactly this.

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION: module resolves to the worktree; 109/0 reproduced; the nine scan-class byte-exact-vs-model on-chip gates re-run green; my own catastrophic mutation (miss-path jump -> HALT) failed the gate in 0.27s proving the harness runs the mutated code; my weaker hand-rolled mutant PASSED and the builder's committed mutant is strictly stronger (it removes the advance AND the cursor write, asserts it really mutates, and is proven wrong-block) — my mutant was a bad discriminator, not a gate gap. Also verified: a HASH_MUL change is invisible to chip-vs-model BY CONSTRUCTION (both sides share the constant) and produces a different-but-valid encoder, so it is not a defect class at all. engine/router untouched; placekyt 1219 re-run post-merge. INV-62 assigned at landing.
